questions.stem: This question is about gases in the atmosphere.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The box gives the names of some gases in the atmosphere. argon carbon dioxide helium nitrogen oxygen Choose gases from the box to answer these questions. Each gas may be used once, more than once or not at all.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Identify a noble gas.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Identify a gas that makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Identify a greenhouse gas.

parts.label: a-iv
parts.text: Identify a gas produced by the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sulfur reacts with oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide gas.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State an environmental problem caused when sulfur dioxide gas dissolves in water in the atmosphere.

questions.stem: The diagram shows the electronic configuration of an atom of an element.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table by giving the missing information about this atom. The table shows the mass number and percentage abundance of each isotope in a sample of this element.

parts.label: b
parts.text: This element has three isotopes. Calculate the relative atomic mass $ \left( A_{\mathrm{r}} \right) $ of this element. Give your answer to one decimal place.

questions.stem: The diagram shows two samples of iron, A and B. Sample B is coated with a thin layer of zinc.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the process used to coat iron with zinc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The two samples of iron are left outside for several weeks. A brown solid containing hydrated iron(III) oxide forms on sample A.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give the common name for the brown solid.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give the names of the two substances that react with the iron to form the brown solid.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Iron can be formed by reacting aluminium powder with iron(III) oxide. The diagram shows how this reaction can be demonstrated. When the magnesium fuse is lit, a very exothermic reaction occurs.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: State the meaning of the term exothermic.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The equation for the reaction between aluminium and iron(III) oxide is $2 \mathrm {A l} + \mathrm {F e} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {3} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {F e} + \mathrm {A l} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {3}$ Explain what this reaction shows about the relative reactivities of aluminium and iron.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Explain why the reaction between aluminium and iron(III) oxide is a redox reaction.

questions.stem: This question is about ionic compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The table shows the formulae of some positive and negative ions, and the formulae of some compounds containing these ions.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Complete the table by giving the three missing formulae.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the name of the compound with the formula $ \mathrm{N H_{4} N O_{3}} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sodium oxide, $ \mathrm{N a_{2} O} $ is an ionic compound. The sodium and oxide ions are held together by ionic bonds.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State the meaning of the term ionic bond.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The diagram shows the arrangement of the electrons in a sodium atom and in an oxygen atom. sodium atom oxygen atom Draw diagrams in the boxes to show the arrangement of the electrons in the ions of sodium oxide. Include the charges on the ions.

questions.stem: The boxes show the displayed formulae of six organic compounds, P, Q, R, S, T and U.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the letters P, Q, R, S, T and U to answer these questions. Each letter may be used once, more than once or not at all.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Give the letter of the compound that is not a hydrocarbon.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the letters of the two compounds that have the same empirical formula.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Give the letter of the compound that is used to manufacture poly(propene).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe a test that can be used to distinguish between compounds Q and T. result with compound Q. result with compound T

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compounds P, Q and R are members of the same homologous series. Give two characteristics of a homologous series.

parts.label: d
parts.text: This is the displayed formula of an alkene, V.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Give the name of alkene V.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Draw the displayed formula of another alkene that is an isomer of alkene V.

parts.label: e
parts.text: An organic compound has the percentage composition by mass C=36.36% H=6.06% F=57.58%

parts.label: e-i
parts.text: Show that the empirical formula of the compound is $ \mathrm{C H_{2} F} $

parts.label: e-ii
parts.text: The relative molecular mass $ ( M_{\mathrm{r}} ) $ of the compound is 66. Determine the molecular formula of the compound.

questions.stem: A student uses this method to investigate the reaction of dilute hydrochloric acid with zinc. pour some dilute hydrochloric acid into a glass beaker record the initial temperature of the acid add a piece of zinc and stir the mixture record the temperature of the mixture after one minute

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a word equation for the reaction of dilute hydrochloric acid with zinc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The diagram shows the thermometer readings for this reaction. Complete the table, giving all values to the nearest 0.1 $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C}. $

parts.label: c
parts.text: Another student repeats the method using five different metals to compare their reactivity.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: This student uses a polystyrene cup instead of a glass beaker. Explain why a polystyrene cup is better than a glass beaker in this investigation.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Give three factors that the student should keep constant in this investigation.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The table shows some of the student's results.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: State why there is no temperature change for copper.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Predict the temperature change for iron.

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: Deduce the order of reactivity of the five metals.

questions.stem: This question is about some of the halogens and their compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which element is a liquid at room temperature? A astatine B bromine C chlorine D iodine

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Which element has the palest colour? A astatine B bromine C chlorine D iodine

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Which element is the least reactive? A astatine B bromine C chlorine D iodine

parts.label: b
parts.text: A teacher uses displacement reactions to demonstrate the reactivities of some halogens. She adds solutions of chlorine, bromine and iodine separately to three different sodium halide solutions. The table shows some of the teacher's results. A change in colour of the solution indicates that a reaction has occurred.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Complete the table by predicting the missing results.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State why the teacher does not add bromine solution to sodium bromide solution.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: The word equation for the reaction of bromine with sodium iodide is bromine + sodium iodide $ \rightarrow $ iodine + sodium bromide Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A technician sees an unlabelled bottle containing a liquid. He knows that the liquid is a solution of one of these compounds. copper(II) chloride copper(II) bromide iron(II) chloride iron(II) bromide Describe chemical tests that the technician could use to identify the compound in the solution.

questions.stem: (a) Carbon dioxide changes directly from a solid to a gas without becoming a liquid. (i) Give the name of the change of state from solid to gas. (ii) Describe the test for carbon dioxide gas.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Carbon dioxide is a simple molecular covalent substance. Explain why carbon dioxide turns from a solid to a gas at a very low temperature.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Diamond and graphite are both giant covalent substances made up of carbon atoms. diamonds are used in cutting tools graphite is used in pencils to make marks on paper Explain, with reference to structure and bonding, why each substance is suitable for its particular use.

questions.stem: A student uses this apparatus to investigate the heat energy released when a liquid fuel is burned. This is the student's method. measure the mass of the spirit burner and fuel add 100 $ cm^{3} $ of water to the copper can record the temperature of the water use the spirit burner to heat the water until the temperature rises by $ 3 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ immediately measure the new mass of the spirit burner and fuel

parts.label: a
parts.text: Suggest why the student measures the mass of the spirit burner and fuel immediately after heating the water.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When the fuel is burned, the student notices that a black solid forms on the bottom of the copper can.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Identify the black solid.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain why the black solid forms.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the heat energy change, Q, to raise the temperature of $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of water by $ 3 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ is approximately 13 kJ. [mass of $ 1. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of water=1.0 g] [c for water = 4.2 J/g/ $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $]

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The student burns 0.96 g of methanol, $ \mathrm{C H_{3} O H} $ Calculate the molar enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , in kJ/mol, for the combustion of methanol. Include a sign in your answer. [M $ _{r} $ of methanol=32]

parts.label: d
parts.text: The table shows data book values for the molar enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , for the combustion of some alcohols with different numbers of carbon atoms per molecule.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Plot the data values from the table on the grid. Draw a straight line of best fit.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Deduce the value of $ \Delta H $ for an alcohol with six carbon atoms per molecule. Show on the graph how you obtained your answer.

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: State the relationship between $ \Delta H $ and the number of carbon atoms per molecule.

questions.stem: Nitric acid $ \left( \mathrm{H N O}_{3} \right) $ is used in the production of fertilisers. Nitric acid is manufactured in three stages. Stage1 ammonia reacts with oxygen in the presence of a platinum catalyst to produce nitrogen monoxide gas, NO, and water. Stage 2 nitrogen monoxide gas reacts with more oxygen to produce nitrogen dioxide gas, $ \mathrm{N O_{2}}. $ Stage 3 nitrogen dioxide gas reacts with water to produce nitric acid and more nitrogen monoxide gas.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the chemical equation for the reaction in stage 1. $\mathrm {N H} _ {3} + \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {N O} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the meaning of the symbol $ \rightleftharpoons $

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: State the purpose of the platinum catalyst.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give a chemical equation for the reaction of nitrogen monoxide and oxygen in stage 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The equation for the reaction in stage 3 is $3 \mathrm {N O} _ {2} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {H N O} _ {3} + \mathrm {N O}$ Calculate the maximum mass, in tonnes, of nitric acid that could be produced in this reaction from 11.5 tonnes of nitrogen dioxide. [1 tonne = 1.0 $ \times10^{6} $ g]

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Suggest what use can be made of the nitrogen monoxide gas formed in stage 3.

parts.label: d
parts.text: When copper(II) oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, copper(II) nitrate is produced. The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {C u O} + 2 \mathrm {H N O} _ {3} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u} \left(\mathrm {N O} _ {3}\right) _ {2} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ 0. 200 mol of nitric acid reacts with excess copper(II) oxide. A mass of 15.3 g of copper(II) nitrate is produced. Calculate the percentage yield of copper(II) nitrate. [ $ M_{\mathrm{r}} $ of copper(II) nitrate=187.5] $\text {T o t a l f o r Q u e s t i o n 1 0 = 1 2 m a r k s)}$
